summary: Yuen Ren Chao was a scholar in linguistics and sinology. He studied at Tsinghua, Cornell, and Harvard. He held positions at Cornell (~1920-1921), Tsinghua (~1925-1929), Harvard (~1941-1946), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1947-1963).
Yuexia was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He founded Huayan University, where he also served as a teacher.

Yuguang Liu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Bsam gtan, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Jialuo, and earned a PhD from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from ~1965 to 1974. He later served as president of Taisho University from ~2011 to 2015.
Yui Chi Lau was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Yingguang Qu. He founded the Vajrayana Esoteric Society and taught Shek-Wing Tam.

Yui Suzuki works in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. Suzuki studied at the University of California, Los Angeles under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

Yuichi Kajiyama worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and the University of Vienna. His posts included Kyoto University (1956-1988), Bukkyo University (1988-1997), and Soka University (1997-2001).

Yuishin Ito studied at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University. A scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, he held posts at Bukkyo University (1961-1997), Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (1997), and Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen (~2000-2008), among other institutions.
Yujiro Motora was a scholar in philosophy who studied at Johns Hopkins University in 1885. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1888-1912) and Tokyo University of Education (~1890-1900).

Yujun Endo was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held positions at Taisho University, including associate professor (attested 1991) and professor emeritus (attested 2014), and served as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014).
Yuka Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held part-time lecturer posts at Ryukoku University (attested 2015) and Hanazono University (attested 2015).

Yukari Kimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed doctoral studies under Kenyo Mitomo and holds posts with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and Rissho University (attested 2026).

Yukei Matsunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Koyasan, Tohoku, and Kyushu universities, and served as director at Koyasan University in 1983 as well as holding a post at Shuchiin University.

Yuki Sasaki is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Sasaki has held part-time lecturing positions at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).

Yukihiko Asayama is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Asayama held posts as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as an overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).
Yukihiko Matsumura works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Matsumura studied at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and held a post there as an expert researcher (attested 2026).

Yukihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn. He held posts at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College (attested 1996, 2015) and Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Yukihisa Yamao was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from ~1954 to 1962 and later held a post there from ~1976 to 2006.
Yukio Hattori was a scholar in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University and held a post at Japan Women's University.
Yukio Kotani is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Hanjiro Tominaga and became an emeritus professor of comparative literature at Rissho University (attested 2001).
